topic: Why do we remember Lord Shaftesbury?
rationaleNote: One heroCallouts sheet (the teacher's kept shape): Shaftesbury's portrait with the lesson's own work and learning changes, including the older-boys limit, kept for Lesson 5, where the teacher points at it to explain why children's time out of work changed. The significance steps (sc-001), the John Pounds comparison and the 1944 name change stay on the board because Lesson 5 asks about change, not significance; the only edit is 'He' made 'Shaftesbury' in 'He helped support schools that others ran.'

cards.title: Lord Shaftesbury
cards.heroCaption: Lord Shaftesbury campaigned with others to protect children through laws.

groups.title: Work
items: It banned underground work for women, girls and boys under ten.
Boys aged ten and over could still work underground.

groups.title: Learning
items: Ragged schools gave poorer children a chance to learn without paying school fees.
Shaftesbury helped support schools that others ran.
